learn.title: Not always equal
learn.body: An inequality compares two expressions that are not necessarily equal. The symbols are $<$ (less than), $>$ (greater than), $\le$ (less than or equal to) and $\ge$ (greater than or equal to). The open end of the symbol points to the larger number.

learn.title: Many solutions
learn.body: An equation like $x+2=7$ has one solution. The inequality $x+2<7$ has many: any number below 5 works. The solutions are $x<5$. On the number line we show this with an open circle at 5 and an arrow to the left. A closed circle means the number is included.

learn.title: Solve $x+2<7$
learn.body: Solve it like an equation: subtract 2 from both sides.
steps: Test $x=4$: $4+2=6$, which is less than 7. True.
Test $x=5$: $7<7$ is false, so 5 is not included.

learn.title: Solve $2x\ge 8$
steps: Test $x=4$: $8\ge 8$ is true, so 4 is included.

learn.title: The one new rule
learn.body: When you multiply or divide both sides by a negative number, flip the inequality sign. From $-2x<6$ we divide by $-2$ and get $x>-3$. Check $x=0$: $0<6$ is true, and $0>-3$ is true.
Test a number to check your answer. A value inside the solution should make the original inequality true.

questions.prompt: Which symbol means "greater than or equal to"?
questions.explanation: $\ge$ combines greater than with the equals bar underneath.

questions.prompt: Solve $2x\ge 8$. What is the smallest whole number that works?
questions.explanation: $x\ge 4$, so 4 is included and is the smallest whole number.
$5+2=7$, and 7 is not less than 7. The boundary is not included.
Dividing by a negative number flips the sign: $x>-3$.

questions.prompt: Solve $3x-1>8$. Put the steps in order.
questions.explanation: Solve like an equation. The sign stays the same because we divide by a positive number.
